newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, no upside seen near-term.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, no upside seen near-term.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 2.1 percent on Monday and traders said the decline could continue for months if foreign investors failed to return to the market.
"The bourse market is almost dead due poor liquidity that may continue until international investors return," said Toni Apollonio, an analyst of bank A banka.

The Bank of Slovenia five weeks ago checked foreign investment by saying international investors would have to open custodian accounts at Slovenian banks in order to trade in Slovenian securities. Since then the blue-chip index has fallen by 17.7 percent.
The banks said they would open first custodian accounts at the end of March.
* The 11-share SBI index fell 29.17 points to 1,361.82.
* Bank SKB was most actively traded, down 2.45 percent to 53,700 tolars on volume of 1,542 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
